items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: In the band was Arthur Bowie, a pianist, John Collins and Stanley Payne, alto sax, Joe Garland, tenor. On drums Burt .........

ctx.x: Sometimes at the dancing school if there were not many men in the place, the manager would open the front windows on Broadway and give Monnegue a sign to tell Ted to blow out for a while. Then Johnny would be kind-hearted enough to call a number that we did not have to read and Ted would blow so loud that he could be heard for five blocks in any direction.

After a few months with Johnny Monnegue I left and went to another dancing school and worked with a leader named Bobby Neal. Bobby was a little fellow about 4 feet tall who played a double-B tuba which was the biggest tuba made. It was much easier playing a dancing school job with Bobby than it was with Monnegue because we played many numbers that we did not have to read. And Bobby would do a little show by walking through his tuba and twirling it around the floor. In the band was Arthur Bowie, a pianist, John…

Bobby was working in a small dancing school on the east side of town, but a big school opened on Broadway over the Strand Theater and was called the Strand Ballroom. Bobby was engaged to play the Strand, so he hired Frank Newton and a trombone player named Jonas Walker. That augmented the band to 9 pieces and this job became the easiest dancing school job in New York because another band was also engaged.
